item.text: {"question_id":"5B.10","answer":"The 2023 evidence does not demonstrate that Lula left a stronger and durable economic trajectory than inherited. There were ruler-attributed or government-attributed steps toward inclusion and state capacity: social and human-rights programmes were reintroduced, new ministries were created, and Minha Casa, Minha Vida resumed with reported deliveries and contracts benefiting lower-income households (BATCH-0016-E003, BATCH-0016-E013). Environmental and climate institutions also received expanded attention and resources, although some evidence concerns broader Lula III reconstruction or comparisons with 2019 rather than outcomes attributable specifically to 2023 (BATCH-0007-E009, BATCH-0007-E012). Aggregate 2023 conditions were mixed: GDP grew, inflation and unemployment declined, and real earnings increased, but these outcomes are not causally isolated to Lula and occurred alongside higher public debt and a larger pension deficit (BATCH-0009-E013). Distributional and household evidence remains adverse or incomplete: 28.8 million children remained in multidimensional poverty, more than 70 million people experienced food insecurity, 39 million workers were informal, and major education, sanitation, housing, racial, and gender disparities persisted (BATCH-0017-E004, BATCH-0001-E020, BATCH-0001-E021, BATCH-0001-E022). Implementation and durability were also uncertain: the TCU identified substantial CadÚnico inconsistencies, weak monitoring, costly regional-development policies with little delivered development, and tariff-policy weaknesses; these findings often concern inherited or institution-level problems and do not establish personal presidential causation (BATCH-0003-E008, BATCH-0005-E010, BATCH-0005-E011). Older baseline evidence further indicates structural fiscal, productivity, infrastructure, education, and planning constraints, but it cannot by itself establish Lula’s inherited-to-left change (BATCH-0019-E015, BATCH-0019-E016). The best-supported conclusion is therefore a mixed, partly improving first-year trajectory with meaningful inclusion measures but no demonstrated durable transformation; implementation lags, external and inherited conditions, institutional constraints, and attribution prevent a stronger
